sources.label: Battery cost
sources.source: Modo Energy 2026 Capex Survey: containerised BESS cost per MWh (GB median; range 4h to 2h median)
sources.quote: Sheet 'By region', row GB, 'Container $/MWh' = 133510.08; sheet 'By duration', 'Containerised BESS $/MWh': 2h (1.5-2.5h) = 151427.03, 4h (3.5-4.5h) = 128229.41
sources.derivation: USD to GBP at 1.3563 USD/GBP (Bank of England XUDLUSS, 9 Sep 2026, the survey's publication day), rounded to £100: low 128229.41/1.3563, mid 133510.08/1.3563, high 151427.03/1.3563

sources.label: Power conversion and balance of plant
sources.source: Modo Energy 2026 Capex Survey: PCS + balance of plant per MW (grid connection excluded; the model prices the cable separately)
sources.quote: Sheet 'Summary', cost stack (all durations): PCS median $/MW 98742.05, mean 115488.98; Balance of plant median 193021.78, mean 191987.01. Sheet 'Cost stack by region', Europe: PCS 39.23, Balance of plant 62.22 ($k/MWh). Note in sheet: 'cost-line medians are independent and do not sum exactly to the total median.'

sources.label: Operating cost
sources.source: Modo Energy 2026 Capex Survey: annual opex (median, p10, p90; some responses include the optimiser fee)
sources.quote: Sheet 'Opex': 'Median $/MW/year' 20000; '10th percentile $/MW/year' 8447.18; '90th percentile $/MW/year' 44942.51; 'Includes optimiser fee' 28405.25; 'Excludes optimiser fee' 12985.26
sources.derivation: USD to GBP at 1.3563: 20000/1.3563, 8447.18/1.3563, 44942.51/1.3563, rounded to £100. Global survey, not GB-only

sources.label: Connection cable (33 kV)
sources.source: NGED South West Statement of Methodology and Charges for Connection, June 2026, section 7.44 cable charges, 33kV additional metres of mains cable
sources.quote: 'Extension of 33kV mains cable' - 'Additional metres of mains cable m': prepared trench 241 / 524; typical footpath or carriageway 225 / 841; unmade ground 154 / 355 (columns 'Min Max', £ per metre)
sources.derivation: low = unmade ground min £154/m x 1000; high = footpath or carriageway max £841/m x 1000; mid = (low + high)/2. Excludes traffic management, wayleaves and final connection (paras 7.46-7.48)

sources.label: Cable route detour
sources.source: PLACEHOLDER - team modelling choice (screening rule of thumb), no published source

sources.label: Crossing uplift
sources.source: PLACEHOLDER - team modelling choice, no published source. NGED's cable table prices carriageway and unmade ground separately, which could replace this uplift

sources.label: Queue fee (OTCF)
sources.source: Ofgem CMP470 minded-to consultation: Oversubscribed Technologies Commitment Fee (proposed, not in force)
sources.quote: para 3.18: 'The OTCF would be introduced at £3,000/MW and reviewed every six months. Where oversubscription has not reduced sufficiently, the OTCF would first increase to £5,000/MW and then in £5,000/MW increments every 6 months up to a maximum of £25,000/MW.'

sources.label: Queue oversubscription
sources.source: Ofgem CMP470 minded-to consultation: BESS operational + Gate 2 capacity vs Clean Power 2030 requirement
sources.quote: Executive summary: 'presently around 90GW of operational and Gate 2 Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) capacity currently exists, against an estimated Clean Power 2030 requirement of around 29GW by 2035.'
sources.derivation: (90 - 29) / 29 = 210% above the requirement. Para 2.5 gives the split: 7GW operational + ~83GW Gate 2

sources.label: Debt share
sources.source: Gresham House Energy Storage Fund: senior project finance for three GB BESS projects, May 2026
sources.publisher: Gresham House Energy Storage Fund plc
sources.quote: 'This financing includes £141 million in senior debt from a syndicate of four lenders, covering up to 70% of project costs, with repayment profiles of at least 15 years and legal maturities of 10 years, priced at 250bps over SONIA.'

sources.label: Interest rate
sources.source: SONIA (Bank of England) + 250bps senior margin (Gresham House, May 2026); low = SONIA + 160bps export-credit facility
sources.publisher: Gresham House Energy Storage Fund plc; Bank of England
sources.quote: Gresham House: 'priced at 250bps over SONIA' and 'Export credit agency-backed facilities ... at a fixed rate priced off SONIA + 160bps' (interim results, 23 Sep 2026, https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/gresham-house-energy-storage-fund--grid/interim-results-for-period-ended-30-june-2026/9785600). Bank of England IUDSOIA 22-23 Sep 2026: 3.7305
sources.derivation: mid = 3.7305 + 2.50 = 6.2305; low = 3.7305 + 1.60 = 5.3305; rounded to 2 dp. SONIA from https://www.bankofengland.co.uk/boeapps/database/_iadb-fromshowcolumns.asp?csv.x=yes&Datefrom=01/Sep/2026&Dateto=26/Sep/2026&SeriesCodes=XUDLUSS,IUDSOIA,IUDBEDR&CSVF=TN&UsingCodes=Y&VPD=Y&VFD=N

sources.label: Arrangement fee
sources.source: PLACEHOLDER - legacy value, not verified. No public UK BESS arrangement fee found; lenders do not disclose upfront fees in RNS announcements

sources.label: Loan term
sources.source: Gresham House Energy Storage Fund: senior project finance, May 2026 (amortisation profile 15+ years, legal maturity 10 years)
sources.publisher: Gresham House Energy Storage Fund plc
sources.quote: 'The facilities each have a repayment profile of at least 15 years, and the legal maturity is 10 years.'

sources.label: Discount rate
sources.source: Listed GB BESS fund NAV discount rates: Gresham House WADR (Q1 2026), Gore Street WADR (FY to Mar 2026); high = Gresham House levered rate
sources.publisher: Gresham House Energy Storage Fund plc; Gore Street Energy Storage Fund plc
sources.quote: Gresham House: 'Weighted average discount rate (WADR) is 10.36% for the full portfolio compared to 10.33% at 31 December 2025.' Gore Street (https://www.gsenergystoragefund.com/content/news/archive/2026/150726.asp, 2026-07-15): 'a slight increase in the weighted average discount rate to 10.25%'. Gresham House HY trading update (https://www.investegate.co.uk/announcement/rns/gresham-house-energy-storage-fund--grid/trading-update-for-hy-results-to-30-june-2026/9750396): 'the discount rate applied to levered cashflows will be one percentage point higher than on unlevered projects.'
sources.derivation: high = 10.36 + 1.00 (levered). The model discounts equity cash flows after debt service, which is the levered case

sources.label: Project life
sources.source: PLACEHOLDER - legacy value, not verified. No public GB lithium-ion BESS asset-life assumption found. Context only: Ofgem LDES cap and floor contracts run 25 years, which is a support term, not an asset life

Capacity market: £11,913/MW/year (4h basis), committed data, published 2026-03-12. Method: clearing price per kW of de-rated capacity x 1,000 kW per MW; the stack then multiplies by the storage de-rating factor for the duration. Period: delivery year 2029/30 (T-4 auction held 10 March 2026). Source: Capacity Market T-4 auction for delivery 2029/30 (auction monitor report, Deloitte for DESNZ).

Balancing ancillary: £24,525/MW/year (4h basis), live. Method: mean clearing price of each service over the period, Low + High frequency sides stacked for one symmetric MW, weighted by cleared volume across DC/DM/DR, x 8,760 h, x participation share = mean cleared MW / GB operational battery MW (REPD); same for every duration. Period: delivery 2025-09-29 to 2026-09-29. Source: NESO EAC auction results (Dynamic Containment, Moderation, Regulation).

Wholesale: £80,363/MW/year (4h basis), live. Method: upper bound: perfect foresight, one full cycle per day; per day (mean of the top d hours' price - mean of the bottom d hours' price) x d MWh per MW x round-trip efficiency 0.85, summed over the days; charge and discharge hours are not forced into order. Period: 2025-09-29 to 2026-09-28 (364 complete settlement days). Source: Elexon Insights, Market Index Data (APX), half-hourly GB prices.

Falcon Park, Wilsons Road - Solar Farm & Battery Energy Storage: 20 MW battery, Application Submitted (as of 2025-06-27), 4.63 km from the site; planning application 25/02539/FUL at South Cambridgeshire. Source: REPD Ref ID 17859, spreadsheet row 12435.

National planning policy under NPS EN-1 and NPPF Chapter 14 establishes a strong national need for energy storage to support grid decarbonisation and security, with jurisdiction retained by the local planning authority under the 2020 NSIP carve-out order regardless of capacity. Within 5 km of the site, local planning precedent includes an application submitted on 27 June 2025 for Falcon Park, Wilsons Road (repd-17859), comprising a 20 MW solar farm and battery energy storage project located 4.63 km away. Proposals are required to comply with NFCC guidance by providing a Battery Safety Management Plan addressing thermal runaway and emergency access, while Planning Practice Guidance requires appropriate landscape mitigation, acoustic fencing, and environmental screening.
